body: Forward test of the valuation-temperature method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.45 (naive base rate 0.48) that: Titan's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return. Evidence: Yahoo close 20-Nov-2026: Titan ₹4,620.0 (52-wk ₹3,751–5,187); Nifty 50 25,800.6. Screener: P/E 57.7 on TTM EPS ₹79.22 (consolidated) vs FY-end P/E (May price ÷ FY EPS) of ~79×, 83×, 86×, 98×, 77× for FY22–FY26 → ~0.7× its own 5-yr median ('cooler than usual'). But TTM earnings are flattered: Q2 FY27 standalone OPM 15% vs 10–11% history included a ~₹490 cr customs-duty gain in jewellery (normalised Titan Jewellery margin 11.1–11.7% per the 11-Nov-2026 call) and gold MTM swings; Q2 standalone sales growth slowed to +8%; coins/investment buying soft. Reasoning: Valuation-temperature test with a twist: the stock looks cool on reported TTM earnings, but on normalised margins the multiple is close to its usual level. If the method only works on clean earnings, it should not help here; we lean slightly under base. Resolution: YES if (Titan NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 4,620.0) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored. Source: NSE / Yahoo Finance closes (TITAN.NS, ^NSEI). Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A single Nifty-50 large cap beats the index over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%).
data.resolution_rule: YES if (Titan NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 4,620.0) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored.

title: Paper call: Titan's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return
